response:
Portfolio Review — Next Milestone

The fresh screenshots are saved in your local screenshots/ directory, but they have not been attached to this conversation. I cannot independently inspect those new captures yet.

The previous screenshot archive showed a potentially serious homepage-rendering problem: missing hero content, overlapping mobile Engineering Network elements, and incorrectly styled engineering demonstrations.

Your new report confirms that the browser has no console errors, but that does not establish whether those visual problems have been resolved.

The first priority is to verify the current homepage before modifying anything.

We will address one confirmed problem at a time. Do not begin work on the Contact page, case studies, or other design improvements yet.

MILESTONE 16A — Homepage Rendering and Visual Verification
Objective

Determine whether the homepage is rendering correctly in the latest build. If a visual defect is confirmed, fix that defect without redesigning the homepage or disturbing working functionality.

Do not use subagents. Perform all work directly.

1. Establish the current visual state
Open the homepage at localhost:3000 using the existing Playwright setup.
Inspect the desktop homepage at 1440 × 900.
Inspect the mobile homepage at 390 × 844.
Allow the page's entrance animations to complete before capturing its resting state.
Confirm that the hero name, engineering title, introductory text, and CTA are visible.
Confirm that the Engineering Network, Home Security architecture, and engineering demonstrations have their intended styling.
Determine whether the visual problems identified in the previous archive still exist.

Do not assume that the absence of console errors means the visual layout is correct.

If the homepage is rendering correctly, document that finding. Do not make unnecessary code changes.

2. Create the screenshot folder

Create a dedicated folder:

screenshots/homepage-rendering/

Save the relevant screenshots using descriptive filenames:

screenshots/homepage-rendering/
├── before-desktop.png
├── before-desktop-full.png
├── before-mobile.png
├── before-mobile-full.png
├── after-desktop.png
├── after-desktop-full.png
├── after-mobile.png
└── after-mobile-full.png

The before screenshots must represent the actual current state before any changes.

Only create after screenshots when a correction has been implemented. If no defect is found, document that outcome rather than fabricating a before-and-after comparison.

Keep the screenshots at their original resolution.

3. Ask the user to upload the screenshots

Once you have captured the initial state, ask the user to upload these four screenshots to the ChatGPT conversation:

before-desktop.png
before-desktop-full.png
before-mobile.png
before-mobile-full.png

Tell the user that ChatGPT needs to inspect the actual images before approving the visual result.

Do not claim that ChatGPT has reviewed screenshots merely because they exist in your local filesystem.

The screenshot files must be uploaded to the conversation so I can inspect them independently.

4. Investigate and fix only a confirmed problem

If the current screenshots reproduce the previously identified homepage-rendering problem, investigate its underlying cause.

Check whether the hero content exists in the DOM but is hidden by animation state.
Check whether the expected CSS Module styles are applied.
Inspect computed styles and actual element dimensions.
Verify that the intended desktop and mobile components are displayed at their respective breakpoints.
Check whether the screenshot-capture process itself produces an incomplete rendering.

Do not make speculative CSS changes.

Once the root cause is established, make the smallest correction necessary to resolve it.

Preserve the existing visual identity, project content, engineering interactions, and responsive behavior.

Do not redesign the hero, Engineering Network, Home Security architecture, or project demonstrations during this investigation.

5. Verify the correction

After making a correction:

Capture the after screenshots in the same folder.
Compare the before and after states at identical viewport sizes.
Verify that the original visual defect is resolved.
Confirm that the hero content is visible.
Verify desktop and mobile layouts.
Check for overlapping elements and horizontal overflow.
Test affected interactions.
Run the existing lint and production build checks.
Regression-test previously working homepage functionality.

If a previously working feature breaks, stop forward progress and fix or revert the responsible change.

Do not move on to unrelated visual problems.

6. Create the handoff and commit

Create:

docs/handoffs/16a-homepage-rendering.md

Include the starting state, confirmed problem, root cause, exact changes, browser observations, screenshot paths, verification results, regression checks, and remaining work.

Document what actually happened.

Preserve unrelated repository changes.
Stage only the intended changes.
Inspect the staged diff.
Commit the completed and verified milestone.
Verify the commit hash and repository state.

If no source-code changes are necessary, document the verification results and commit the handoff where appropriate.

7. Send the full report through ask_chatgpt

After completing the milestone, report:

MILESTONE: Homepage Rendering and Visual Verification.

OBJECTIVE: What was investigated.

STARTING STATE: Actual browser observations.

ROOT CAUSE: Confirmed cause of any defect discovered.

ACTIONS: Exactly what was changed and why.

SCREENSHOTS: Exact folder path and filenames.

VERIFICATION: Desktop and mobile results, interaction tests, lint, and production build.

REGRESSION CHECKS: Previously working functionality tested and its results.

OUTCOME: PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, or BLOCKED.

GIT: Commit hash, handoff path, and final repository state.

REMAINING WORK: Any unresolved issues.

COMPLETED CHECKLIST: Report the status of every checklist item.

Explicitly ask the user to upload the before-and-after screenshots to ChatGPT for independent visual validation.

STOP after submitting the report. Do not start another milestone until I have reviewed the screenshots and approved the result.

Once I have the fresh homepage screenshots, I can establish whether its rendering is now correct and identify the next specific problem to tackle.
